issues.legal_issue: An oral intimation to a party’s counsel that an arbitration award has been filed can constitute notice and start the limitation period for challenging the award.
material_facts: The arbitrator filed the award in court, and the court adjourned the matter for the parties to state their position on the award.
The parties’ pleaders were present when the court recorded that the matter was adjourned for their response to the award.
The appellant’s guardian later knew that the award had been filed and sought time to object, but filed the objection after the applicable limitation period.
issues.conclusion: The court’s intimation to the parties’ pleaders that the award had been filed was sufficient notice; the objection was out of time.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 158 of the First Schedule to the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, the limitation period for an application to set aside an award runs from service of notice of its filing. Section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, requires the court to give notice of filing but does not require written notice; intimation may be oral. Under Order III, Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, notice to a party’s pleader is presumed to be communicated to the party. Section 42 of the Arbitration Act, which concerns service of notice by a party or an arbitrator, does not govern notice given by a court. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: The proceeding concerns a party’s challenge to an arbitration award filed in court.
predicates.court_orally_informed_party_or_counsel_o: The court orally informed the party or the party’s counsel that the award had been filed.
predicates.objection_filed_after_applicable_limit: The party filed the objection after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from the notice of filing.

issues.definition: When an award challenge involves court-given oral notice of filing to a party or counsel and the objection is filed after the applicable limit, the objection is time-barred.

issues.legal_issue: An order directing an arbitration award to be filed and a decree to be drawn in its terms is not an appealable refusal to set aside the award when no party sought to set it aside.
material_facts: The appellant’s objection to the award was filed after the limitation period.
The court directed that the award be filed and a decree be drawn in its terms.
There was no timely objection before the court seeking to set aside the award.
issues.conclusion: The order was not an order refusing to set aside the award, so no appeal lay under section 39(1)(vi) of the Arbitration Act, 1940.
issues.legal_principle: Section 39(1)(vi) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, permits an appeal from an order refusing to set aside an award. Where no party has sought to set aside the award, there can be no refusal to grant that relief and no appeal under that provision. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_order_concerning_arbitration: A party brought an appeal from a court order concerning an arbitration award.
predicates.no_party_sought_to_set_aside_award: No party before the court sought an order setting aside the award.
predicates.court_directed_award_to_be_filed: The court directed that the award be filed.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns an order on an arbitration award, no party sought to set the award aside, and the court directed that it be filed, the appeal cannot be maintained as an appeal from a refusal to set it aside.

issues.legal_issue: An objection to an arbitration award that was not pressed before the trial court may be treated as abandoned and disallowed on appeal.
material_facts: The appellant contended that the arbitrator had included property outside the scope of the arbitrator’s authority.
That objection was not pressed before the trial court.
The High Court did not permit the objection to be raised on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to disallow the objection because it was not pressed before the trial court and was presumed to have been given up.
issues.legal_principle: An objection not pressed before the trial court is presumed to have been abandoned and need not be allowed to be raised for the first time on appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_concerning_arbitration_award: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an arbitration award.
predicates.objection_not_pressed_before_trial_court: A party did not press the objection before the trial court.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning an arbitration award, an objection not pressed before the trial court may be treated as abandoned and not entertained on appeal.
